title: Genitive: Exceptions & Edge Cases
titleRussian: Родительный падеж: исключения и особые случаи
description: The standard genitive rule covers most nouns, but three families slip through: 3rd-declension feminines, -мя neuters, and meaning-overrides-ending masculines. This lesson teaches them.
descriptionRussian: Стандартное правило родительного падежа охватывает большинство существительных, но три группы выпадают: третье склонение (женский род на -ь), слова среднего рода на -мя и мужские слова с «женским» окончанием. Этот урок посвящён им.
intro: Every exception in this lesson is an old acquaintance. The soft-sign feminines, мать and дочь, the -мя neuters, the male-person nouns that end like feminines: you met all of them in the very first book of this level, when they were breaking the gender rules. Here they are breaking a case rule instead. That is worth knowing, because it means Russian keeps a small standing cast of difficult words rather than an endless supply.
rules: 3rd-declension feminine (-ь): feminine nouns ending in soft -ь take -и in the genitive, not -ы. Тетрадь → тетради. Ночь → ночи. Кровать → кровати. Площадь → площади.

Stem extension for мать and дочь: these two 3rd-declension feminines insert -ер- before the ending. Мать → матери. Дочь → дочери. This pattern repeats across every case form (матери, матерью, etc.); only the nominative singular hides it.
-мя neuters: a small closed group of neuter nouns ending in -мя inflects from an -ен- stem. Время → времени. Имя → имени. Same for пламя, племя, семя.

Meaning-overrides-ending masculines: nouns like папа, дядя, дедушка, мужчина look like feminine -а nouns and decline like them (genitive: папы, дяди, дедушки, мужчины), but they refer to men, so every adjective and pronoun stays masculine (мой папа, нет моего папы).
examples: У меня нет тетради. (I don't have a notebook.) тетрадь → тетради, 3rd-declension feminine, -ь → -и.
До поздней ночи. (Until late at night.) ночь → ночи, 3rd-declension feminine, -ь → -и.
У моей матери. (At my mother's place.) мать → матери, 3rd-declension feminine with -ер- stem extension.
У дочери нет книги. (My daughter doesn't have a book.) дочь → дочери, -ер- stem extension.
У меня нет времени. (I don't have time.) время → времени, -мя neuter, -ен- stem.
Я не помню её имени. (I don't remember her name.) имя → имени, -мя neuter, -ен- stem.
У папы нет машины. (Dad doesn't have a car.) папа → папы, declines like feminine -а but masculine in gender.
Подарок для дяди. (A gift for uncle.) дядя → дяди, -я → -и; masculine in gender.
Чашка чая. (A cup of tea.) чай → чая, regular soft-stem masculine genitive (-й → -я).

items.hint: Тетрадь ends in soft -ь and is feminine. Does feminine -ь take -ы or -и in the genitive?
items.explanation: Тетрадь is a 3rd-declension feminine (feminine -ь). The genitive ending is -и, not the -ы you might expect from analogy with the -а class. So тетрадь → тетради. The same rule covers ночь → ночи, кровать → кровати, площадь → площади.

items.hint: Мать is 3rd-declension feminine AND inserts -ер- before the ending.
items.explanation: Мать is one of only two nouns (мать, дочь) that insert -ер- between the stem and the ending. So the genitive is матери. The construction 'У + genitive' triggers the case as usual; the irregularity is in the stem extension.

items.hint: Время is a -мя neuter. The stem extends with -ен- before the ending.
items.explanation: Время belongs to the small -мя neuter group (время, имя, пламя, племя, семя). They inflect from an old stem in -ен-: время → времени. 'У меня нет времени' (I don't have time) is one of the most-used Russian phrases.

items.hint: Папа ends in -а. What do feminine -а nouns become in the genitive?
items.explanation: Папа ends in -а, so it declines exactly like a feminine -а noun: -а → -ы → папы. But meaning overrides ending: every adjective and pronoun stays masculine (мой папа, нет моего папы). The shape follows the ending; the gender follows the meaning.

items.hint: Имя is a -мя neuter. Same pattern as время.
items.explanation: Имя is the other very common -мя neuter. Same -ен- stem: имя → имени. The verb помнить ('to remember') with negation takes the genitive of the thing forgotten.

items.promptEnglish: This is a gift for uncle.
items.hint: Дядя ends in -я. What does soft feminine-shape -я become in the genitive?
items.explanation: Дядя declines like a feminine -я noun: -я → -и → дяди. The preposition для triggers the genitive (Lesson 6). Дядя refers to a man, so the gender stays masculine, even though the ending shape says 'feminine class.'

items.hint: Чай is a soft-stem masculine. What ending replaces -й in the genitive?
items.explanation: Чай is a regular soft-stem masculine: -й → -я, giving чая. Чашка takes the genitive: чашка чая.

items.hint: Ночь is 3rd-declension feminine. Same rule as тетрадь.
items.explanation: До triggers the genitive (a preposition not in your Lesson 6 list, but it works the same way). Ночь is 3rd-declension feminine: -ь → -и → ночи.

items.hint: Дочь is in the same tiny club as мать: insert -ер-.
items.explanation: Дочь is the second of the two stem-extension nouns: дочь → дочери. The -ер- shows up across every case form (дочери, дочерью, etc.); only the nominative singular hides it. There are only two such nouns in the whole language; once you know мать/дочь you've covered the set.

blanks: У меня нет _____. (I don't have time.)
У _____ нет книги. (Mother doesn't have a book.)
Это подарок для _____. (This is a gift for dad.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Three different exception classes in one drill: -мя neuter (время → времени), 3rd-declension feminine with stem extension (мать → матери), and masculine-that-looks-feminine (папа → папы, but gender stays masculine).

minimalPairs.explanation: The regular feminine pattern would predict 'тетрады' (-а → -ы), but тетрадь is 3rd-declension feminine. Its genitive ending is -и, not -ы. Тетрады is not a Russian word.

Папа ends in -а and declines like a feminine -а noun: in the genitive, папа → папы. The gender stays masculine (we say 'мой папа,' not 'моя папа'), but the case form is built from the noun's ending shape.

errorCorrection.sentence: В этой комнате нет дверь, только окно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This room has no door, only a window.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дверь is a 3rd-declension feminine (soft -ь), and after нет it must take the genitive -и: двери. Дверь left unchanged is the nominative.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это подарок для дедушка на день рождения.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a birthday gift for grandpa.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дедушка names a male person but ends in -а, so it declines like a feminine -а noun while staying masculine in agreement. Для requires the genitive: дедушки.
Мужчина is one of the meaning-overrides-ending masculines: grammatically masculine (этого, not этой) but it declines like a feminine -а noun. After 'у', the genitive is required: мужчины.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это подарок для юноша, который любит спорт.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a gift for a young man who loves sports.
errorCorrection.explanation: Юноша is masculine in meaning but ends in -а, so it declines like a feminine -а noun: nominative юноша → genitive юноши. Для requires the genitive. The same shape applies to папа, дядя, дедушка, мужчина.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: A lamp stands next to the bed.
errorCorrection.explanation: Кровать is a 3rd-declension feminine (soft -ь), and около requires the genitive: около кровати. The bare кровать is the nominative, left undeclined.

patternRecognition.question: Why does тетрадь become тетради and not тетрады?
options: Because тетрадь is 3rd-declension feminine (-ь class), which takes -и, not -ы.
Because of the husher spelling rule.
Because the genitive of all feminine nouns is -и.
patternRecognition.answer: Because тетрадь is 3rd-declension feminine (-ь class), which takes -и, not -ы.
patternRecognition.explanation: Feminine -ь nouns belong to a separate declension class and take -и in the genitive. This is independent of the husher spelling rule (which is why книги and ночи look similar but for different reasons).

patternRecognition.question: What kind of noun is имя, and what shape does its genitive take?
options: A -мя neuter; genitive built on the -ен- stem: имени.
patternRecognition.answer: A -мя neuter; genitive built on the -ен- stem: имени.
patternRecognition.explanation: Имя is one of the small -мя neuter group. It inflects from an old stem in -ен-, so the genitive is имени, the dative will be имени, and so on across the case forms. Время behaves the same way.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the possessive моего (masculine) but the noun ending is -и (feminine-looking)?
options: It is a mistake; should be у моей дедушки.
Дедушка ends in -а, so it declines as a feminine-shape noun, but gender follows meaning (a man), so the possessive stays masculine.
The possessive doesn't agree with дедушка.
patternRecognition.answer: Дедушка ends in -а, so it declines as a feminine-shape noun, but gender follows meaning (a man), so the possessive stays masculine.
patternRecognition.explanation: This is the meaning-overrides-ending pattern. The noun shape says 'feminine class,' so it takes the -а → -и ending, but the meaning ('grandfather') is masculine, so мой/моего/моему all stay masculine. Same for папа, дядя, мужчина.

reviewVocab.definition: third declension (the small feminine class ending in soft -ь: тетрадь, ночь, кровать, мать, дочь)
reviewVocab.example: Тетрадь, ночь, мать — слова третьего склонения.

reviewVocab.definition: time (a -мя neuter; genitive is времени, not время)
first name (a -мя neuter; genitive is имени, not имя)
mother / daughter (the only two nouns in Russian that insert -ер- between the stem and the ending: матери, дочери)
reviewVocab.example: У матери, у дочери — везде появляется -ер-.
